articles.title: Pop Loser: W.W.J.J.D? (What Would Joan Jett Do?)
articles.author: Audrey Vann
paras: Welcome back to Pop Loser! This week, we’ll honor our lord and savior, Joan Jett, who turned 68 on Tuesday. It was a slow news week, so I’ll dive into that weird time in the ’80s when rock musicians tried rapping. Plus, a Macklemore update, a new book from Michelle Zauner, and some much-needed wisdom from Laurie Anderson.

Happy birthday, Joan Jett! Seriously, she’s probably the reason I care about music at all. My Joan Jett obsession began sometime in middle school, when I saved up my babysitting money to buy Cherie Currie’s memoir Neon Angel at the Westwood Village Barnes & Noble. I, who otherwise hated reading, devoured that book. It catapulted me into an obsession with the Runaways, David Bowie, Suzi Quatro, and Jett’s own solo career. As time went on, I found her to be unexpectedly attached to any and all newfound obsessions, like The Gits (Jett fronted the band Evil Stig with members of the Gits to raise money to investigate former frontwoman Mia Zapata’s murder) and Bikini Kill (Jett produced their single “Rebel Girl.” (Also see: Kathleen wearing the iconic W.W.J.J.D? shirt .) All roads worth travelling lead to Joan Jett.

Remember that time Joan Jett tried rapping? I am slightly embarrassed to say that at one point in my life, my favorite Joan Jett song was her 1986 venture into hip-hop, “Black Leather,” which I unironically adored. She raps, “Late at night while the normals rest / I feel real wicked when I start to dress / my clothes, they stare at me, like they want to make love to my body.” At that point, I knew two things: I never wanted to be one of the “normals,” and that I needed a leather jacket stat.

Jett wasn’t the only rock icon who tried rapping in the ’ 80s… It’s a phenomenon I think about often. There’s the good (Blondie’s “ Rapture ”), the so-bad-it’s-good (Lou Reed’s “ The Original Wrapper ”), and the ugly (Dee Dee Ramone’s solo career as Dee Dee King ). As much as I hate to admit it, Aerosmith actually had the right idea by collaborating with Run-DMC for “ Walk This Way ,” instead of trying to take on the emerging genre themselves.

CD revenue is up by nearly 60% in the first half of 2026. According to a report from the Recording Industry Association of America, CD sales have increased by 58.6% during the first six months of the year, reaching $171 million. By comparison, vinyl sales climbed a more modest 2.4%.

Macklemore makes a compelling case for separating the artist from the art—because the artist is good, but the art is bad. This week, our hometown hero announced he will be donating his earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to Palestinian aid, writing, “I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom.”

Meanwhile, Ed Sheeran has proven himself to have zero redeeming qualities. Sheeran launched into his Philadelphia show on Saturday by attempting to clarify his stance on the genocide in Gaza and Macklemore’s removal from the tour. He read the speech off a teleprompter: “I have tried in my career not to be a political commentator of any kind because I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division, about humanity, not politics.” In other words, a long-winded way of whining, “Please don’t be mad at me!”

If you found yourself Googling Billy Joel on Thursday, don’t worry— he’s alive ! Fans were concerned after a glitch in the search engine listed the Piano Man’s date of death as September 17, 2026. “Billy’s not dead,” the singer’s publicist, Claire Mercuri, confirmed. “I was just emailing with him.” (I’ll admit, that last part wasn’t exactly convincing.)

Michelle Zauner (aka Japanese Breakfast) announced her new memoir, Thank You for Your Suffering . The follow-up to the acclaimed debut Crying in H Mart comes out April 27, and documents the year Zauner lived abroad in South Korea, immersing herself in the language and culture to connect with her late mother’s family.
Now, take a deep breath and enjoy… Laurie Anderson shares her and her late husband Lou Reed’s three rules to live by.

I’m doing great, can’t you tell? Fiona Apple’s songwriting does the most compelling thing songwriting can do: putting words to seemingly indescribable feelings. Her music is something I return to when I’m looking for emotional clarity. Lately, my favorites are “Oh Well,” “Get Gone,” and “Valentine.”

articles.title: Slog AM: Wilson Announces Budget, Boy vs. Bear, Gen Z Is Not Masturbating
articles.author: Nathalie Graham
paras: Lorax mode: A grassroots conservation organization has successfully saved a fuckload of trees on the Olympic Peninsula. After the Department of Natural Resources sold a 74-acre plot of state forest to Webster Logging, the Elwha Legacy Forests Coalition made a proposition: What if the group paid the loggers what they would make from chopping down the trees… but they didn’t chop down any trees? Webster Logging said sure. The group has managed to raise $563,000 and protect 29 acres of trees so far . The Lorax wishes he were this effective, but he is not very business-minded.
Ex-Xboxers: As part of the 3,200-employee layoff Microsoft announced in July, 268 Xbox employees in Washington state lost their jobs .

Bellingham boy battles bear: A mama bear came face-to-face with 12-year-old Robin Westgate in his family’s Bellingham backyard. She charged him twice , clawing his side and leaving puncture wounds on his hip. Robin fought back, punching, screaming, and gouging the bear’s eye with his thumb. His little sister, Riverly, heard the screams and went for help. His dad appeared. The bear charged him and bit down on his hand right as he landed “the hardest punch of my life.” The bear ran off.
A quick note from The Stranger’ s Cedar Attanasio, who tuned into Mayor Katie Wilson’s budget speech:

Facing a $175 million budget deficit , Mayor Katie Wilson announced a proposed plan to balance the city’s books, a $9.1 billion austerity budget. She wants to cut city services and keep taxes as they are, all while funding 66 more police officers. She said it’s time to get the city’s budget in order and not kick cost-cutting down the road. She’s kicking tax increases, like, say a city capital gains tax, down the road. What’s next? The city council is expected to weigh in on how to cut between one and eight percent from city departments.
And, Seattle banned algorithmic pricing in grocery stores: Read the story here .

Grand Illusion finds new home: The beloved Grand Illusion Cinema, which left its University District home in 2025 after 50 years, is moving back to the neighborhood to take over the recently closed Varsity Theater . That’ll give the Grand Illusion, which used to only have one screen, three screens to play with. After a few improvements , the plan is to open up in November or early December and show movies every day of the week.

World Cup cash: The FIFA World Cup officially brought in $889 million in total economic impact to Seattle this summer. That includes $109 million in state and local tax revenue. While the reality was about $40 million less than original estimates, that’s still a buttload of money. The city is considering it a win. It was a mixed bag for businesses.
The climate: Extreme heat from this year’s extreme El Niño will likely cause 450,000 deaths worldwide in the next six months.

FBI hacked: Hacker group ShinyHunters claims it has breached the FBI and now holds personal data on all 5,000 FBI members. Embarrassing. The hackers also defaced the FBI jobs website, writing “this site has been seized by ShinyHunters” on it and announcing they’d collected personal data from the feds. Their MO is to attack targets and then extort them, but this time is a little different. “What we plan to do is not something I’d call extortion, maybe coercion,” one of the hackers told 404Media. ShinyHunters claims the FBI made “false claims” in an official report about the hacking group. The hackers are giving the FBI one week to “correct” or remove the report.

At his UN visit, President Donald Trump told a CNN journalist , “You should not be here.” He went on: “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me… You said you weren’t going to cover me.” That’s not what happened. Trump said CNN wasn’t going to cover him. He banned CNN along with MS NOW and Politico from the White House and removed them from White House pool duties, prompting a wave of news organizations to refuse pool duties in an act of solidarity. The banned outlets sued on Monday.

A US District judge will hold a hearing today. articles.title: Zahilay Announces More Than $19.5 Million in New Housing Investments
articles.author: Ryan Packer
paras: King County Executive Girmay Zahilay unveiled a proposed $19.5 million in new funding for permanent affordable housing and transitional shelter on Monday, a major milestone toward achieving a goal of building 500 new units within his first 500 days in office. The budget proposal came at the same time that Zahilay announced new public private partnership between King County and the Schultz Family Foundation that is expected to result in another $10 million investment over the next three years to directly address youth homelessness.
The Urbanist's Fall Member Drive is in full swing! Support our work, read ad-free, and help us hit our goal for the member drive!

Some of the new funding would come from a potential countywide 0.01% sales tax set to be taken up by the King County Council later this week. Directly authorized by the state legislature earlier this year, the dedicated funding source is targeted at services that benefit children and families. If approved, it would generate approximately $10.3 million in 2027 for King County.

However, that amount could diminish in the future if other cities across the county opt to use the same sales tax authority to fund services of their own due to a provision capping the total that can be levied in any one jurisdiction at 0.01%.

"I think that there is no issue that is of a greater priority to our administration or to the public at large than affordable housing," Zahilay said Monday, announcing the funding package at a press event at the Mary's Place Family Center in Seattle's Denny Regrade. "And so if there's any issue that we should be spending our money on, even during constrained budget periods, I think it's this one."

Out of the $19.5 million, $5 million is earmarked for a new 80-unit tiny home village in the Central District, to be sited in an underutilized corner of the Judge Patricia H. Clark Children and Family Justice Center campus at 12th Avenue and E Spruce Street. The facility would be run by the Low Income Housing Institute (LIHI) with 24/7 staffing, on-site amenities, and 30 homes set aside for families with children.

The City of Seattle has been leaning heavily on LIHI to help achieve Mayor Katie Wilson's ambitious goals around expanding shelter capacity, targets that were recently scaled back to 1,000 new units of shelter by the end of 2027. Earlier this month, LIHI broke ground on a 20-unit tiny home village with space for an additional 72 RVs in West Seattle, on a site owned by the Washington State Department of Transportation.
The Spruce Street site would be LIHI's first tiny home village on King County property.

"Over the years, we've had City-owned property, Port-owned property, and private property, even Sound Transit property, and so we're thrilled for the first time to have property from King County," Sharon Lee, LIHI's Executive Director, told The Urbanist following the press conference. "It's on vacant site. It's been sitting vacant for many years, and now it's going to be transformed into a tiny house village with 80 tiny houses, including families with children, as well as singles and couples and people with pets. So we're very excited about this, and we hope to get going right away."

Other new dollars announced by Zahilay will assist affordable housing projects that are already in the works. For example, $4 million will fund 18 two and three-bedroom units at the Pacific Tower Quarters Buildings in Beacon Hill, adding to $1.5 million that King County already allocated to the project. Intended to be an intergenerational affordable housing campus, the Quarters project requires coordination between the Pacific Hospital Preservation and Development Authority and the Seattle Chinatown International District Preservation and Development Authority, and involves retrofitting existing structures that were originally built to house medical staff at the 1933 U.S. Public Health Service Marine Hospital.

Additionally, $3 million would be put toward a new joint development between Mercy Housing Northwest and Mary's Place along Ambaum Way in Burien. Planned with 200 shelter beds – replacing 150 that Mary's Place previously operated on the site – the project also includes approximately 90 units of permanent affordable housing, 30 of which are being set aside for families who are directly exiting homelessness.
Earlier this summer, the portion of the site being constructed by Mary's Place topped out, on track for a 2027 opening.

Mary's Place will also receive $2.4 million to keep the 140-unit shelter in Seattle's former Glen Hotel on Third Avenue open. Without that funding, King County would have been poised to lose those beds, even as Mary's Place opens new beds on the Mercy Housing Campus in Burien.

A $1.8 million allotment is tabbed for 100 transitional housing units for veterans in Kirkland, part of the larger Veterans Service Hub that is being funded through the County's Veterans and Human Services Levy.

And finally, King County is committing an unspecified amount to a long-planned affordable housing project in the International District. Located on the site of a former gas station, the 701 S Jackson Street development is advancing as a public-private partnership with O.Z. Navigator – a collaboration between the developers Nitze-Stagen and the Housing Diversity Corporation. Plans currently call for 111 total units to be built on the site, with site remediation already completed.

On top of those County investments, the matching dollars from the Schultz Family Foundation are intended to maintain existing 12 shelter beds and bring on another 80 specifically targeted at children and young adults. According to King County, around 1,000 residents under 18 years old are currently experiencing homelessness with a severe shortage of shelter specifically available for that youth population.

Zahilay told reporters that the County looks to be on track to achieve the goal of building 500 units of some type of subsidized housing in 500 days that he set back in March , as part of his administration's "Breaking the Cycle" initiative. Those units could lay the groundwork for an even larger, countywide housing levy that Zahilay floated earlier this year, with a report due by the end of the year laying out that potential measure's feasibility.

"Housing continues to be the challenge of our time," District 2 Councilmember Rhonda Lewis said at Monday's announcement. "Finding affordable housing is an uphill battle for families in all parts of King County, and some families are facing a greater struggle than others. Whether it is due to medical issues, financial strain, unexpected changes of events, we have neighbors who don't have housing. In this time of history, in this country, this is unacceptable."
Zahilay is expected to release the rest of his proposed budget, an update to an already approved two-year county budget, this Thursday.

articles.title: Friday Roundtable: Quiet Zone in Kent
articles.author: Michael Smith
paras: On August 24, 2026, Kent’s long-awaited Quiet Zone took effect along the BNSF Railway mainline through downtown. This designation, granted by the Federal Railroad Administration in June , no longer requires trains to sound their horn when approaching an at-grade crossing. Over the past 14 years, the City of Kent has worked to meet the necessary requirements to achieve a Quiet Zone. Recent infrastructure upgrades include building raised concrete medians, adding additional signs, and refreshing pavement markings. In a non-Quiet Zone area, all trains are required to sound their horn 15-20 seconds before each street crossing.

The BNSF mainline tracks are used by 38 passenger trains and many more freight trains every day. The frequent at-grade crossings in downtown Kent resulted in nearby residents hearing hundreds of train horns day and night. The Quiet Zone stretches between S 212th St and S 259th St. The following crossings are included:

As safety is still a top priority, train engineers are still allowed to sound the horn in emergency situations or as they deem necessary. While the Quiet Zone is officially in effect, it may take some time for nearby residents to hear a difference. One week after the change was implemented, the Kent Reporter noted that many trains were still using their horn at each crossing. I was in Kent earlier this week and each of the five trains (four Sounder, one Amtrak Cascades) I saw used their horn at each crossing.

articles.title: Cafe Lolo Is the Neighborhood Restaurant Every Neighborhood Deserves
articles.author: <name>Kat Thompson</name>
paras: If I were to describe the perfect neighborhood restaurant, Cafe Lolo would completely fit my definition. The food is comforting and nourishing, emphasizing local ingredients, which playfully come together in a way that feels both fresh and familiar. The space is draped in natural light that’s assisted by over a dozen lamps. The inviting dining room is covered in quirky Renaissance-inspired murals that don’t feel disruptive. There are to-go meal kits available for purchase, as well as local beers. It’s an atmosphere that invites you to unwind with a bottle of wine. Owners Leah Engel, Alex Halmi, and Brett Bankson are present, not only flitting about the room, but also cooking the dishes in the kitchen and laughing with customers. If I lived in the neighborhood, just off the main drag of Capitol Hill, it’s somewhere I’d want to return to over and over again.

Cafe Lolo has an extensive wine menu and many local beers, as well as bottles in the fridge you can pick up to-go. Although yes, the wine list — which includes just one glass from Washington, and more options from Oregon and Europe) — is worth perusing, the nonalcoholic tisanes are also made from seasonal ingredients. The strawberry rhubarb soda I had on my visit was effervescent and floral without an overpowering sweetness.

Like the rest of the menu, dessert will change pending seasons — but don’t skip it. My visit included a celebration of ripe, macerated strawberries over a semolina olive oil cake, which had a buttery crust and a tender interior crumb. There was also a scoop of rhubarb sorbet; light, sweet, and sharp.
